role.altitude: The adapted PE specialist keeps teaching, encouraging and adjusting exercises for each pupil and judging progress; looking up goals, planning from scratch, computing test scores and drafting report text shrink.
reach: Class teachers and intern support staff
skills_to_grow: Recording short, specific progress notes that reports can build on
role.ambitious_version: A specialist whose reports write themselves from the term's notes, leaving time for one more lesson a week.

tasks.short: Provide students positive feedback during lessons to encourage them and help them develop an appreciation for physical education, and note progress worth celebrating.

steps.what: Adapted PE specialist provides students positive feedback during lessons to encourage them
Adapted PE specialist notes progress worth celebrating in the pupil record

tasks.design: Encouragement stays fully personal. Notable progress is noted on a tablet with a short pick list per pupil goal in the pupil record, so it can feed reports later. The progress note belongs to the records task 25-2059.01:17008 and is priced there; encouraging pupils does not change.
tasks.previous_blocker: Nothing blocked it; this is teaching.
tasks.enabler_now: Pupil records with quick notes on tablets.
tasks.still_hard: Pupils who have had bad experiences with sport.
tasks.human_edge: Finding the words that make a pupil try again.

reach.learn: Whether shared progress notes help in class.

evidence.claim: A pupil record system tracks learning goals and support plans.

assumptions: Boundary: encouragement in lessons and notes about it.
s2 is the specialist's first note of progress worth celebrating and keeps its full time.

incremental.description: No upkeep in this task; keeping the progress pick list current is counted with sibling task 25-2059.01:17008.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: No saving in this task: the only changed step, noting progress, belongs to the records task 25-2059.01:17008.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Review pupils' goals and support plans, plan adapted lessons, provide individual or small groups of students with adapted physical education instruction that meets their needs and goals, and note progress.

steps.what: Adapted PE specialist reviews each pupil's goals and support plan
Adapted PE specialist plans the adapted lesson for the group
Adapted PE specialist provides adapted physical education instruction to individual students or small groups
Adapted PE specialist notes progress against each pupil's goals

tasks.design: A lesson view in the pupil record shows the movement goals and relevant support-plan notes of every pupil in the group, instead of opening each plan. Lessons are planned from the specialist's library of exercises with adaptations by impairment. Teaching stays fully in the gym. Progress against goals is ticked on a tablet with a short note.
tasks.previous_blocker: Goals had to be looked up per pupil and lessons rebuilt each time.
tasks.enabler_now: Goal views in pupil records and exercise libraries.
tasks.still_hard: Pupils whose needs change from day to day.
tasks.human_edge: Adapting an exercise on the spot so a pupil can succeed.

reach.learn: Whether shared goals align school and therapy.

evidence.claim: In a randomised trial, teachers using a planning assistant cut weekly preparation from 3.3 to 2.5 hours, but used it for few lessons.
A support plan is set within six weeks of enrolment and evaluated yearly.

assumptions: Boundary: preparing and giving adapted lessons; setting support plans is the school's care team's.
Input contract for s1: goals and support-plan notes kept in the pupil record by the care team.
s4 is the specialist's first note of progress against each pupil's goals and keeps its full time.
research_questions: Do lessons match goals more often?

incremental.description: Adapted PE specialist adds new adaptations to the exercise library.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few pupils with stable goals; high: many pupils with detailed support plans.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Set up equipment, instruct students using adapted physical education techniques to improve fitness, gross and perceptual motor skills or sports achievement, observe and adjust, and record motor test results.

steps.what: Adapted PE specialist sets up equipment and stations
Adapted PE specialist instructs students using adapted physical education techniques
Adapted PE specialist observes performance and adjusts the exercise
Adapted PE specialist records motor test results

tasks.design: Instruction, observation and adjustment stay fully in the gym. Motor test results are entered on a tablet during the test, and the system computes the age-norm scores instead of looking them up on paper tables afterwards. No software judges the pupil.
tasks.previous_blocker: Test results were written on paper and scored from norm tables later.
tasks.enabler_now: Tablet forms with norm tables built in.
tasks.still_hard: Pupils who cannot do a standard test.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing which small step a pupil is ready for.

reach.learn: Whether scored tests are available sooner.

evidence.claim: AI that evaluates learning outcomes is AI Act high-risk; norm scoring here is a fixed table.

assumptions: Boundary: instruction and testing in lessons; reports are a separate task.
Instruction and observation keep their full time.
unknowns: How often motor tests are done.

incremental.description: Adapted PE specialist updates norm tables when a test version changes.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few tests; high: test weeks with many pupils.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Gather test results and progress notes, judge overall progress, write reports to summarize student performance, social growth or physical development, check and sign them and share them with parents.

steps.what: Adapted PE specialist gathers test results, notes and goal progress for the report
Adapted PE specialist judges each pupil's overall progress
Adapted PE specialist writes reports to summarize student performance, social growth and physical development

loop.input: The specialist's progress notes, test results and overall judgement for one pupil.
loop.output: A draft report comment in the school's template.
loop.check: Each sentence must trace to a note, a result or the specialist's judgement; no diagnostic labels; the specialist rewrites what does not fit.
loop.stop: The specialist signs, or writes the comment by hand after two redrafts.
loop.why_not_simpler: Comments must be personal and readable for parents.

steps.what: Adapted PE specialist checks and signs the final report
Adapted PE specialist shares the signed report with parents in the school system

approvals.approved_version: the report as signed by the specialist in s4; any change needs a new signature

tasks.design: The report template pulls the pupil's motor test scores and goal progress from the pupil record, so the specialist no longer gathers them from spreadsheets. The specialist judges overall progress. A drafting step writes a first comment from the specialist's own notes and judgement, with each sentence traced to a note or result and no diagnostic labels; the specialist rewrites, signs and shares the report. No software assesses the pupil.
tasks.previous_blocker: Reports were assembled from scattered notes and written from scratch.
tasks.enabler_now: Pupil records with goal tracking and drafting tools with source checks.
tasks.still_hard: Writing honestly about slow progress in a way parents can hear.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing growth that no test score shows.
tasks.altitude: Less assembling and drafting; judgement stays.

reach.learn: Whether reports are clearer to them.

evidence.claim: Science teachers using a chatbot with a guide cut weekly planning by 31% with no quality difference.
AI that evaluates learning outcomes is AI Act high-risk; the design drafts text only from the teacher's own judgement.
Staff consent is needed for tools that can monitor them, and parents for pupil-data rules.

assumptions: Boundary: writing and sharing pupil reports; parent meetings are outside.
Input contract for s1: test results and progress notes recorded by the specialist in lessons and kept in the pupil record; about 80% of report data come from there; s1 is priced at that share.
Judging, signing and sharing keep their full time.

already_counted.description: Adapted PE specialist rewrites drafted comments.

incremental.description: Adapted PE specialist keeps the report template current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few pupils with sparse notes; high: many pupils with good notes through the term.
